subject: Linguistics
title: Dead and Extinct Languages
description: A micro-lesson that makes Dead and Extinct Languages usable.

hook.text: Latin isn't really dead—it lives on as French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, and Romanian.

buildup.text: A dead language has no native speakers; an extinct language has no speakers and no derivatives.

discovery.text: Sumerian, Hittite, and Etruscan are extinct—they left no living descendants at all.

twist.text: Latin's 'death' is really transformation—it didn't vanish, it evolved into multiple new languages.

climax.text: Even truly extinct languages leave traces—loanwords, place names, and inscriptions preserve fragments.

punchline.text: Languages don't always die—sometimes they just change their name.

quiz.question: How does a dead language differ from an extinct one?
options: Dead languages may have living descendants; extinct ones don't
